clue.text: Screen rock legend holding his head in empty theatre

indicators.note: the rest of the wordplay goes in between the theatre's remaining outer letters
an empty theatre has its inside cleared out, leaving only its first and last letters
the rock star's name holds his own initial within it

parts.note: Elvis Presley, the king of rock and roll

indicators.note: the head of a name is its first letter

parts.note: 'his' points back to the rock legend, Elvis

explanation.surface: A film about a rock star being screened in a deserted cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his head' is Elvis's head, E, put inside ELVIS to make ELEVIS; 'empty' leaves T and E of theatre, which go around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To screen a programme is to broadcast it, as a station does on its channels.

clue.text: Clue from winner eclipsing Boatman's last

indicators.note: to eclipse is to cover, so the winner encloses the boatman's final letter

parts.note: a hit is a success, a winner

indicators.note: the last of the word boatman is its final letter

explanation.surface: A puzzle hint about a race won by a rower overtaking the boatman.
explanation.definitionFit: A clue and a hint are synonyms: each is a pointer helping someone work something out.

clue.text: In Madrid, the consistent team?

parts.note: el is Spanish for 'the'
even means steady, consistent

explanation.surface: A question whether Real Madrid is the reliable side.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: a football or cricket side has this many players.
explanation.definitionFit: Football and cricket sides field this many players, so the number stands for a team.

clue.text: Electrical device starts to adjust tension 19 fiddled with first

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come first, with the starts placed after them
fiddled means tampered with, so the letters of the other answer are rearranged

parts.note: 19 down's answer, a word meaning the balance or the rest

indicators.note: the starts of the two following words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A dimmer switch whose first letters were adjusted by meddlers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddled' rearranges OTHERS (19 down) into RHEOST; 'with first' puts that ahead of AT, the starts of 'adjust tension'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rheostat is a variable resistor used to control current, such as a dimmer, so it is an electrical device.

clue.text: Appraisal Nutmeg's given in online post?

parts.note: E is the prefix for electronic or online, as in email

indicators.note: the setter's self-reference is placed inside the online post

parts.note: a station is a post, as in a duty station
Nutmeg is this puzzle's setter, so Nutmeg's means 'I am', I'M

explanation.surface: A setter asking for an assessment of her work posted on the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: Nutmeg is the setter, so 'Nutmeg's' is I'M, which goes into E-STATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Appraisal and estimation are both a judgment of worth or size.

clue.text: Supported building, somewhere youth can go, as Spooner might have it

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the initial sounds of the two words are exchanged

parts.note: a teen is a youth
somewhere one 'can go' is a loo, a toilet

explanation.surface: A building with supports, where young people may visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhere youth can go' is TEEN LOO; swapping the first sounds gives LEAN TOO.
explanation.definitionFit: This shed type leans against a wall that holds it up, so it is a supported building.

clue.text: Worked to gain experience under malign influence?

definitions.meaning: a junior barrister who devils does work for a senior to gain experience
playfully, possessed by a devil, as if bedevilled

explanation.surface: A trainee working hard while under some evil spell.
explanation.walkthrough: In the English legal profession, a junior barrister who does work for a senior one is said to devil for them.
explanation.definitionFit: The legal trade sense means did apprentice work; the playful sense means possessed by a demon.

clue.text: Leave European Community, breaking restraint on power

indicators.note: on means after here, so power follows
the community breaks into the restraint, lodging inside it

parts.note: a dam is a barrier restraining water
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Brexit-style news about quitting the EC to break limits on power.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to depart suddenly, so it is a synonym for leave.

clue.text: Army colonel's last two rooms reasonably priced here

parts.note: a host is a great army

indicators.note: the colonel's last two letters are the final pair of that word

explanation.surface: An officer's quarters cheaply priced for the troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostel offers cheap lodging, so its rooms are reasonably priced.

clue.text: All but one of team in Lord's practice session succeeding?

indicators.note: the reduced team sits inside the practice session

parts.note: Lord's is a London cricket ground, and cricketers practise in the nets

indicators.note: the team loses one of its letters, the I

parts.note: XI is eleven in Roman numerals, a cricket team

explanation.surface: A cricket team practising at Lord's, wondering about success.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the famous London cricket ground; a practice session there is in the nets, NET.
explanation.definitionFit: Next means coming after, which is one sense of succeeding, as in the succeeding day.

clue.text: Article added to champion Scot's memorabilia

indicators.note: the article is added after the other pieces

parts.note: a victor is a champion
Ian is a typically Scottish name
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A Scottish champion's collection with an extra item.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoriana is collectable items from the nineteenth-century era of Queen Victoria, a type of memorabilia.

clue.text: Conclusive statement about Irish flyers

indicators.note: about means around, so the final word goes around the Irish abbreviation

parts.note: amen ends a prayer, a statement at the conclusion

explanation.surface: A final word said about pilots from Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmen are pilots and aircrew, people who fly.

clue.text: Jester may take this Scandinavian drink with added extra

parts.note: to take the mickey is to mock, as a jester might
a Finn, from Finland, is loosely counted Scandinavian

explanation.surface: A court fool sampling a Nordic drink spiked with something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take the mickey' is British slang for teasing or mocking.
explanation.definitionFit: This name is for a drink secretly spiked with a drug, so it has an extra ingredient.

clue.text: Hot meal enlivened with a drop of neat alcohol

indicators.note: enlivened means stirred up, so the letters are shaken into a new order
a drop of the word neat is its first letter

explanation.surface: A hot dish livened up by a splash of undiluted spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enlivened' rearranges HOTMEAL together with N, the first letter given by 'a drop of neat'.
explanation.definitionFit: Methanol is wood alcohol, the simplest of the alcohol family of chemicals.

clue.text: Read out two letters too many

indicators.note: spoken aloud, the two letters sound like a word

parts.note: the letters X and S, which when spoken sound like the answer

explanation.surface: An instruction to speak a pair of letters too often.
explanation.definitionFit: An excess is a surplus, a quantity beyond what is needed.

clue.text: We put in hardened seed to produce plant

indicators.note: the word we is put in the hardened word

parts.note: set means hardened, like concrete
a pea is a seed

explanation.surface: Gardeners sowing a tough seed to raise a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The sweet pea is a climbing flowering plant grown for its scent.

clue.text: Faithful man of God admits brief deception

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the saint holds the deception

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the deception loses its last letter

parts.note: a trick is a deception

explanation.surface: A devout clergyman owning up to a little lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Strict and faithful both mean adhering closely, as in a strict adaptation.

clue.text: Addict invested in retro fashion bags

indicators.note: invested means put inside, so the addict goes inside
retro means backwards, so the word sort is read backwards

parts.note: to fashion is to sort, to arrange
a user is a drug addict

explanation.surface: A junkie spending money on vintage clothes and handbags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bags' is old British slang for wide trousers, as in Oxford bags.
explanation.definitionFit: Bags is a dated British term for loose-fitting trousers.

clue.text: Balance books for ladies

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books
hers means belonging to a woman

explanation.surface: Accounts balanced for some women.
explanation.definitionFit: The balance means the remainder, the rest, which is what this word means in 'and the rest'.

clue.text: Quirky novel set in secret hideaway

indicators.note: quirky means odd, so the letters are oddly rearranged

explanation.surface: An offbeat book located in a hidden retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a private place where lovers meet, a romantic hideaway.

clue.text: Impenetrable work leads to awkward questions, upsetting editor

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: the leads of the following words are their first letters

explanation.surface: An obscure book provoking awkward questions that annoy its editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting editor' reads as part of the picture but just gives two more first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Opaque means not letting light through, and figuratively hard to understand, like impenetrable.

clue.text: Hare in poor health close to exhaustion

parts.note: to hare is to run fast
low means unwell, depressed

explanation.surface: A sickly hare near collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplies running low are nearly used up, close to being exhausted.

clue.text: Have the audacity to reject initial synopsis

indicators.note: rejecting the initial drops the first letter of the word

parts.note: to presume is to have the audacity to do something

explanation.surface: An editor boldly rejecting a first summary.
explanation.definitionFit: A résumé is a summary, a synopsis of the main points.

clue.text: Complex first stage for heating engineers?

indicators.note: complex means intricate and mixed up, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A complicated opening phase for heating technicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Gas fitters install and service gas boilers, so they work as heating engineers.

clue.text: Sightseers here perhaps inclined to knock back a little drink

indicators.note: knocking back sends it the other way, so the phrase is read backwards

parts.note: a sip is a small drink

explanation.surface: Tourists tempted to down a quick drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the Leaning Tower: tourists posing there lean as if propping it up.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian city has a famously tilted bell tower where tourists gather and lean.

clue.text: Rome's commoner people brought sandwiches

indicators.note: the two words sandwich the answer between them, holding it inside

explanation.surface: Ordinary Romans bringing packed lunches.
explanation.definitionFit: The plebeians were the common citizens of ancient Rome, as opposed to patricians.

clue.text: Trace sister pinching a case of champagne

indicators.note: pinching means nipping, so the sister holds the letter a

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside letters

explanation.surface: A nun stealing from a box of fizz.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuance is a subtle shade, a slight trace of difference.

clue.text: Reflective nature of mystery plays with mass participation

indicators.note: the mass takes part, so its letter goes into the rearranged word
plays means acts out, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: M is the symbol for mass

explanation.surface: Mystery plays staged with crowds of performers.
explanation.definitionFit: Symmetry is mirror balance, where one half reflects the other.
